question: On the arrival of spring, the village of _____________ resounds with the sweet singing of Bagurumba.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bodo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bagurumba is a traditional folk dance of the **Bodo tribe**, predominantly found in **Assam, India.**
 
• It is performed during the spring season, which marks the arrival of good weather and the blooming of nature.
 
• The dance and singing associated with **Bagurumba **are deeply connected with nature, celebrating the beauty of the surroundings and the harmony of life.
 
• The song and dance are traditionally performed by Bodo women, who dress in traditional attire known as the **'Dokhna, Jumgra and Aronai'.**
 
• Bagurumba is characterized by its elegant movements that imitate the dances of butterflies fluttering in the spring.
 
• This cultural expression is a vital part of the Bodo community's heritage, reflecting their reverence for nature and seasonal changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Khasi**__

 __
 
• The Khasi people are indigenous to the northeast Indian state of **Meghalaya.**
 
• They are well-known for their unique matrilineal society where lineage and inheritance are traced through women.
 
• Their traditional dance includes the 'Nongkrem Dance', which is part of a celebration to honour the deity and secure a good harvest.
 
 
 
• **Garo**__
 __
 
• The Garo tribe is also predominantly found in Meghalaya, as well as parts of** Assam and Bangladesh.**
 
• Their significant festival includes 'Wangala', which is a harvest festival celebrated with dazzling dances and the sounds of drums.
 
• Known for their traditional shamanistic rituals, they uphold a deep connection with nature and ancestral spirits.
 
 
 
• **Karbi**__
 
 
• The Karbi community primarily resides in the** Karbi Anglong district of Assam.**
 
• Their culture includes festivals such as 'Chomkan' and 'Hacha Kekan', which involve elaborate dances and music.
 
• Karbi people speak the Karbi language, which is part of the Tibeto-Burman language family.
